newsitem.title: UK: Monthly review - Fighting rages in Zaire.
newsitem.headline: Monthly review - Fighting rages in Zaire.

text.p: Fighting raged between Zairean troops and Tutsi rebels in October leading to the exodus of thousands of refugees. Aid agencies responsible for feeding more than a million Hutu refugees prepared to evacaute.
The purist Islamic Taleban captured the Afghan capital of Kabul but the ousted government forces fought back alongside northern leader Abdul Rashid Dostum.
Here is a chronology of the main events of the month:
Oct 1 - The Taleban Islamic movement appeals for international recognition as the new government of Afghanistan.
Oct 2 - The moderate National Conference party wins a sweeping majority in the first local elections in Kashmir since a separatist revolt began in 1990.
Oct 2 - A Boeing 757-200 belonging to the Peruvian airline Aeroperu crashes off the Pacific coast north of Lima killing all 70 on board.
Oct 2 - Former Bulgarian prime minister Andrei Lukanov is found shot dead outside his home.
Oct 3 - President Bill Clinton signs a proclamation suspending entry into the United States by Burma's government leaders.
Oct 3 - Serbia and Bosnia agree to open full diplomatic relations.

Oct 3 - Wislawa Szymborska of Poland wins the 1996 prize for Literature. Other Nobel winners: Oct 7 Australian Peter Doherty and Swiss Rolf Zinkernagel (Medicine); Oct 8 British professor James Mirrlees and Canadian William Vickrey (died Oct 11) (Economics); Oct 9 U.S. scientists David Lee, Douglas Osheroff and Robert Richardson (Physics); Oct 9 Americans Robert Curl and Richard Smalley and Briton Sir Harold Kroto (Chemistry); Oct 11 Bishop Carlos Filipe Ximenes Belo and Jose Ramos-Horta (Peace).
Oct 7 - Activists raise the national flags of both communist China and Taiwan's exiled Republic of China on an East China Sea archipelago held by Japan.
Oct 7 - IRA bombs Britain's army headquarters in Northern Ireland, injuring 31 people - one of whom died of his wounds on Oct 11. It was the first major bombing incident in the province in two years.
Oct 8 - Palestinian leader Yasser Arafat makes his first public visit to Israel to meet Israeli President Ezer Weizman.
Oct 8 - Pope John Paul has a successful operation to remove his appendix.
Oct 8 - Leading Chinese dissident Liu Xiaobo is ordered to serve three years in a labour camp.
Oct 10 - The first U.S. troops pull out of Bosnia after a 12-month peacekeeping tour.
Oct 11 - OECD votes to admit South Korea as a member.
Oct 11 - Former South African defence minister Magnus Malan is acquitted of murder charges resulting from the killing of 13 blacks in 1987.
Oct 13 - Turkish Cypriot forces shoot and kill a Greek Cypriot who crossed into the north of the island - the fourth killing in the buffer zone since August.
Oct 13 - Anti-Baghdad Kurdish rebels retake the stronghold of Sulaimaniya, a month after losing it to a faction allied with Saddam Hussein.
Oct 13 - Forces of the ousted Afghan government take Jabal-os-Saraj, the front-line headquarters town of the Islamic Taleban.
Oct 13 - Austria's far-right Freedom Party under Joerg Haider wins 28 percent of the vote in Austria's first European elections.

Oct 14 - Belgium's top court removes the magistrate leading an inquiry into the country's child sex abuse and murder scandal from the case. On Oct 20 over 250,000 people march through Brussels in protest.
Oct 15 - Italy's highest appeal court orders a retrial for former SS captain Erich Priebke, overturning the previous verdict.
Oct 15 - Somali warlords declare an end to hostilities at the end of a week of talks at the invitation of Kenyan President Daniel arap Moi.
Oct 16 - At least 81 people are crushed to death at an overcrowded Guatemalan stadium after fans without tickets barged in to see a World Cup soccer qualifying game.

Oct 17 - Russian President Boris Yeltsin sacks security chief General Alexander Lebed. On Oct 19 Yeltsin also sacks Lebed as his personal representative in Chechnya and appoints Ivan Rybkin to take over both posts.
Oct 18 - Ousted Afghan government forces backed by artillery commanded by General Abdul Rashid Dostum capture Bagram airbase from the Taleban.
Oct 18 - Fighting between Zairean troops and ethnic Tutsi rebels flares in eastern Zaire, triggering an exodus of tens of thousands of Hutu refugees.
Oct 21 - Costa Rica, Japan, Kenya, Portugal and Sweden were elected to the U.N. Security Council, effective January 1 1997.
Oct 22 - At least 25 prisoners burned to death in a Venezuelan jail after guards fired tear gas canisters which started a blaze.
Oct 23 - Gro Harlem Brundtland, who dominated Norway's politics for 15 years, announces her resignation.
Oct 23 - Former Zambian president Kenneth Kaunda says he and his party will boycott the November 18 general election.
Oct 23 - Visiting French President Chirac becomes the first foreign head of state to address the Palestinian legislature.
Oct 24 - Boris Yeltsin and Ukrainian President Leonid Kuchma resolve all problems surrounding the disputed Black Sea fleet.
Oct 25 - Defence Minister Igor Rodionov says Russia's armed forces are on the brink of "uncontrollable developments".

Oct 26 - Tutsi rebels seize the towns of Uvira and Rutshuru after two days of battles with Zairean troops. The U.N. evacuate their aid workers from the area. On Oct 30 Rwandan commandos drive Zairean troops from the town of Bukavu and the town's Roman Catholic Archbishop, Christophe Munzihirwa is killed.
Oct 27 - An 11-storey building collapses in Cairo's Heliopolis suburb killing at least 32. Dozens are still missing.
Oct 27 - Police fought running battles with Islamic militants trying to stage a demonstration outside Pakistan's parliament and at least 29 people were reported hurt.
Oct 28 - European Union foreign ministers agree a new law to counter U.S. anti-Cuba legislation.
Oct 28 - In Malta, Labour leader Alfred Sant is sworn in as prime minister by President Ugo Mifsud Bonnici after the Nationalist Party defeat in the general election of Oct 26.
Oct 30 - A Beijing court sentences dissident and former student leader Wang Dan to 11 years in prison.
Oct 30 - A South African court sentences former state assassin Eugene de Kock to more than 200 years in jail, describing him as a chilling and revolting agent for apartheid.
Oct 31 - A Fokker-100 aircraft from Brazil's TAM airline slammed into homes in Sao Paulo, killing all 96 people on board and at least eight on the ground.
Oct 31 - Liberia's chief warlord Charles Taylor says he survived an assassination attempt when gunmen ambushed him inside the presidential palace. A senior aide was killed.

Notable deaths in October included: former Bulgarian prime minister Andrei Lukanov (2nd); former Quebec premier Robert Bourassa (2); French tennis player Rene Lacoste (12); German publisher of Stern magazine Henri Nannen, (13); U.S. film actress Laura La Plante (14); German composer Bertil Goldschmidt (17); leading Algerian novelist Abdelhamid Benhadouga (21); French film director Marcel Carne (31).
